Mrs. Fisher: I can see you’ve already caught a few fishes on your own, I will give you some tips on the best fishing spots.
Mrs. Fisher: If you want to catch big you should stay here, on the coast. The biggest fish around here, the halibut, lives in the ocean, but you need to keep in mind that they often have the most microplastic.
Mrs. Fisher: The other places are the nearby lake and river, but they are also heavily polluted. Industrial plants are dumping a lot of stuff there unsupervised and fertilizer from the fields also gets there through the groundwater.
Mrs. Fisher: Out of three of them, fishes from the river are the safest to consume. Running water tends to be cleaner. There you can catch many freshwater species like bass or trout.
Mrs. Fisher: If we were a little more up north, you could catch salmon in a river too. The biggest fish you can get in the river is the catfish. They can sometimes get really huge, so be careful!
Mrs. Fisher: The lake has the worst water of all these places. It’s muddy and full of algae, but some fishes thrive in this environment. Common fishes there are carp and tilapia.
You: Is there a place with better water? 
Mrs. Fisher: If you are concerned with the quality of the fish you get, you can try going to the fish farm. Catching fish there is not as satisfying as catching one in the wild, but theoretically fish there should be safer to eat.
You: Theoretically? It sounds like you are implying that it’s not the case.
Mrs. Fisher: To make the fish farm more efficient, fish there are getting juiced up with antibiotics and growth hormones. Their diet there is also a bit sketchy.
Mrs. Fisher: The truth is, there’s no safe choice. 
You: That’s kinda depressing…
Mrs. Fisher: Don’t worry, I eat those fish all the time and I’m still kicking.
